title: Money up, output up?

predict.q: The money flow around the economy = price level × volume of output. Nominal GDP rises by 10% and the price level (deflator) also rises by 10%. What happened to real GDP?

options.fb: That is the nominal rise. All of it came from prices.
Price rises are not output. Adding them double-counts the inflation.
Volume 0%: real GDP stays at 1,000 while nominal GDP is 1,100.
Prices rose by the same 10%, so the quantity of output did not change: it did not fall.

task: Move the price-level slider and the output slider until nominal GDP is up 10% with prices up 10%. Watch nominal and real GDP.
takeaway: Nominal GDP can rise with no extra output at all; only real GDP tracks the quantity produced.
explore: Try prices +5% and volume +5%: nominal 1,102.5 (not 1,100), real 1,050.
